He built his fortune by turning around and selling marine-salvage operator Wijsmuller. long_biography.plain_text:
Trained as a lawyer at Leiden University, Muller joined offshore contractor Heerema and led the management buyout of its loss-making salvage subsidiary. He restored Wijsmuller to profitability, sold his stake when Maersk acquired the business and also helped expand and float McGregor Fashion Group.

His enduring project has been Spyker. With designer Maarten de Bruijn, he turned a prototype sports car into an aviation-inspired marque, later taking the company public and into Formula One. Spyker's acquisition of Saab brought Muller international prominence but ended with the Swedish manufacturer's bankruptcy. After repeated restructurings and another Spyker insolvency, he returned with a new limited-production model in 2026.
